newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of PPI.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of PPI.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in lacklustre trade, dealers said on Friday.
They said most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. March producer price index (PPI) and retail sales index data.
The producer price index for March is forecast to be unchanged from a 0.4 percent decline reported in February.
The March retail sales index is expected to ease to 0.6 percent against February's 0.8 percent.
"Rates were narrowly mixed in the morning some position adjustments and weekend booksquaring," a local dealer said.

"Some people are waiting for fresh clues to market direction from tonight's release of the producer price index and retail sales index for March. But the numbers have been built into the market and most people have squared their positions for the weekend, so I don't think there will be much impact," he said.
In day-to-day rates, weekend and Monday/Tuesday eased 1/8 percentage point to a common 5-1/2 5-3/8 percent, respectively.
Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged from Thursday's 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, three-months unchanged at 5-13/16 5-11/16 and twelve-months unchanged at 6-5/16 6-3/16 percent.
